extracted.intended_audience: web developers, content authors, and user-agent/assistive-technology implementers working with MathML
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and normative rules from the MathML 4.0 specification for making MathML content accessible and for characterizing/implementing MathML conformance in processors and user agents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply WCAG principles to MathML content
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) framework (perceivable, operable, understandable, robust) to establish accessibility requirements for digital content containing MathML.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As WCAG provides no direct MathML guidance, this specification defines how to apply WCAG to MathML. Following these recommendations helps satisfy widely used accessibility requirements and expands readership. Additional best-practices live in MathML-Notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Always use MathML markup for mathematical content
rubrics_metrics.description: All mathematics and linear chemical equation content should be marked up using MathML rather than ASCII or static images; even single-letter variables should be MathML elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using MathML ensures consistent audio, braille and visual renderings and allows assistive technologies to access semantic structure. Do not rely on images with alt text where MathML is appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use intent and arg attributes to reduce ambiguity
rubrics_metrics.description: Use MathML's intent and arg attributes (including for blanks and units) to reduce notational ambiguity not reliably resolved by assistive technologies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Intent attribute covers blanks and units. Combine intent annotations with aria-description when useful; make such descriptions visible (e.g., tooltips) so sighted users can access them on demand.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mark invisible operators explicitly
rubrics_metrics.description: Invisible operators (operators not rendered visually but implied) must be marked up in MathML to preserve their semantic meaning for assistive technology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use invisible times (U+2062) for implicit multiplication, function-application (U+2061) for implied function application, invisible comma/separator (U+2063) for omitted commas/argument separation, and invisible plus (U+2064) for mixed-fraction implicit addition. Do not use <mphantom> with an operator (screen readers ignore <mphantom> contents).

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper grouping of sub-expressions
rubrics_metrics.description: Group sub-expressions in MathML the way they are mathematically interpreted (for example using <mrow>).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Correct grouping improves spacing, enables intelligent linebreaking/indentation, and simplifies semantic interpretation for screen readers and text-to-speech tools.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not use spacing elements to convey meaning
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not rely on spacing elements to encode semantics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid using <mspace>, <mphantom>, and <mpadded> to convey mathematical meaning; these elements are for visual spacing and may be ignored by assistive technologies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enclose numeric quantities in <mn>
rubrics_metrics.description: All numeric quantities must be wrapped in an <mn> element; digit-group separators (commas, periods, spaces) should be included as part of the number and not treated as operators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This preserves the semantic identity of numbers for parsing, speech, and braille translation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply superscripts/subscripts to appropriate elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Superscripts and subscripts must be applied to the correct element or sub-expression, not to closing parentheses or other grouping symbols.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorrect application impedes navigation and semantic interpretation by assistive technologies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use element-specific markup for elementary notation
rubrics_metrics.description: Use MathML's dedicated elements for elementary notations (e.g., <mlongdiv>, <mstack>) rather than generic containers like <mtable> when appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For long division and stacked expressions prefer <mlongdiv> and <mstack>. These elements carry semantics and layout more appropriate than misusing <mtable>.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fill-in-the-blanks markup
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate blanks (e.g., underlined spaces for answers) using intent and arg attributes, and provide an id and event hooks for interactive editing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In interactive environments add an id to the blank element and an onclick or similar event to invoke an editor. Details depend on the desired interaction and JavaScript used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose between HTML tables and <mtable> appropriately
rubrics_metrics.description: Use an HTML <table> when rows/columns are semantically related and benefit from robust screen-reader table navigation; use <mtable> for matrices and purely visual math alignment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HTML structural elements offer better table navigation; <mtable> is useful where visual tweaks for alignment are needed without new table cells.

rubrics_metrics.name: Natural-language mathematics handling
rubrics_metrics.description: When instructional materials write math words in natural language (e.g., 'times', 'multiplied by'), these may be ordinary text or marked up as operators where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because words like 'times' read fine by speech engines, markup as <mo>times</mo> is only necessary when you need it treated as a math operator.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide accessible descriptions (aria-description + intent)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide auxiliary accessible descriptions for mathematical constructs using ARIA (aria-description) and intent annotations; make descriptions visible on request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: aria-description allows tagging literal strings on elements and is appropriate for verbose instructional content; pair it with intent. Ensure descriptions are also visible (e.g., via tooltips) so sighted users can access them.

rubrics_metrics.name: User agent must expose MathML in the accessibility tree
rubrics_metrics.description: User agents (browsers) should process MathML into the DOM and expose MathML elements in the accessibility tree so assistive technologies can understand structure and semantics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The accessibility tree should retain MathML information so platform accessibility services can obtain roles/states/properties. If the accessibility API lacks sufficient information, the DOM must be made programmatically available to assistive technologies per UAAG Success Criterion 4.1.4. Include elements like <mspace> when they convey meaning (e.g., for braille) and include mathcolor/mathbackground when color conveys meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support synchronized highlighting and navigation
rubrics_metrics.description: Expose MathML tree structure so assistive technologies can highlight or speak individual elements as users navigate (e.g., arrow-key navigation) and support synchronized highlighting for TTS and braille.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This enables visual highlighting during TTS, braille navigation with synchronized speech, and finer-grained interaction (e.g., refreshable braille + speech).

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations of alttext for MathML
rubrics_metrics.description: alttext can override standard speech processing but has important limitations and should not be relied on for navigation or synchronized highlighting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: alttext must contain the full spoken text (cannot target parts), is plain text only (no speech cues like pauses/pitch), and lacks linkage to the MathML tree (so synchronized highlighting and navigation are not possible). Use intent or aria-description for finer control.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid ARIA labels in MathML (do not use aria-labelledby/arialabel)
rubrics_metrics.description: Placing ARIA labels (aria-labelledby/aria-label) on MathML elements is not appropriate because it can override braille generation and other MathML-specific accessibility mappings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow MathML Accessibility API Mappings guidance instead; do not rely on adding ARIA labels to MathML to provide semantic info.

rubrics_metrics.name: MathML conformance types (input, output, round-trip)
rubrics_metrics.description: Three conformance forms are defined: MathML-input-conformant (accepts all valid MathML), MathML-output-conformant (generates valid MathML), and MathML-round-trip-conformant (preserves MathML equivalence when accepting and producing MathML).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definitions clarify what processors must do: an input-conformant processor must accept valid MathML (it needn't render it); an output-conformant processor must generate valid MathML representing application data; a round-trip-conformant processor must preserve interpretation equivalence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the MathML Test Suite to quantify implementation
rubrics_metrics.description: Characterize which parts of MathML an application meaningfully implements by referencing categories/examples from the official MathML test suite.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Developers are encouraged to itemize omitted parts by referring to specific test-suite categories. Customers should use the test suite to verify vendor claims; the W3C MathML Validator helps validate output.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deprecated-feature rules for conformance
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules clarify how deprecated features affect conformance: output-conformant tools may not generate deprecated features; input-conformant tools must support deprecated features to claim conformance with MathML 1.x/2.x (but not required for 4.0); round-trip conformance only requires equivalence on expressions without deprecated features.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should avoid generating deprecated markup. Tools that need to claim backward compatibility should document support for deprecated features.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension mechanisms and their conformance implications
rubrics_metrics.description: MathML defines extension mechanisms (mglyph, maction, definitionURL/content dictionaries) to encode concepts beyond the current spec; MathML makes no conformance requirements on the use of extensions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extensions allow experimental ideas but are not required or restricted by conformance. Prefer standard Unicode code points when they become available (e.g., an mglyph used today should be replaced by the Unicode point when standardized).

rubrics_metrics.name: MathML validity requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A valid MathML expression is an XML construct determined by the MathML RelaxNG Schema plus the additional requirements in the specification; a MathML processor must accept or produce valid MathML expressions to be considered conformant in the relevant sense.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A validating parser claiming MathML-input-conformance needs only accept valid expressions; it may not need to render or interpret them. Different application types (validators, editors, renderers, CA engines) have different practical expectations.
